Hirebotics adds line tracking and linear rails to extend cobot capabilities

New features help cobots paint moving parts and reach larger workpieces, bringing more flexibility to production lines.

The Robot Report ↗19 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 3

Moving parts and larger workpieces

Hirebotics introduced line tracking for conveyor-based painting and a modular linear rail at IMTS 2026 in Chicago. Both use the Beacon platform as their main interface, extending the range of tasks its cobots can handle.

Painting without stopping the conveyor

Sensors detect the workpiece and an encoder tracks conveyor movement. The system adjusts the painting path as the part moves. Operators teach the direction and configure the task in Beacon; the company says conventional programming is not required.

Extending the working envelope

The cobot has a reach of about 1.75 metres. Rail sections add roughly 1.5 metres at a time, with custom lengths also available. This can help with long structures or difficult-to-move parts in welding, plasma cutting and painting applications.

Available features and future plans

At the time of publication, operators repositioned the rail manually. Hirebotics planned to add position confirmation in Beacon and targeted automatic rail movement for late 2026. Those planned capabilities should be distinguished from features already available.
